seen_animation: a.png frame 1: a drawn bird with its head folded onto its back, an oval body and one straight leg with a small Z-shaped knee and a horizontal crossbar, stands right of centre in front of grey fence posts and a grey tree trunk; its right side is cut off by the frame edge. Frames 2-4: this bird slides right and leaves the frame, while the curved back of a second, identical bird comes in at the left edge. Frames 5-6: the second bird slides in further from the left until its whole body, head and leg are visible; the grey scenery slides right with it. Frames 7-16: the second bird stands on its one leg near the left third of the frame and does not move; the scenery stays fixed.
seen_film: d.png frame 1: a pink flamingo is cut off at the right edge, standing behind a wire fence with a tree trunk at top centre. Frames 2-4: the camera pans left; the right flamingo slides out at the right edge and a second flamingo, head tucked into its back, slides in from the left edge, while the tree moves right. Frames 5-8: the second flamingo comes fully into view, standing on one leg, as the pan slows. Frames 9-16: the camera settles with only a small drift; the flamingo stands asleep on one leg near the left third of the frame and does not move.
named_subject: a flamingo sleeping on one leg with its head tucked onto its back (two flamingos are seen during the pan)
evidence: Judged from still frames only, not playback. e.png 1-5 against f.png 1-5: the first bird sits at about 75-99% of the panel width in frame 1 and moves right to about 93-99% by frame 5, then is gone in frame 6, as the right flamingo in the film is. e.png 2-8 against f.png 2-8: the second bird's back appears at the left edge in frame 2 and its right edge advances step by step (about 4%, 8%, 13%, 17%, 21%, 24%, 28% of panel width), close to the film's flamingo entering at the same rate, with no reversals. e.png 9-26 against f.png 9-26: the bird holds near the left third with a slight rightward drift over 9-13 that matches the film's pan settling, then holds still while the film holds. g.png shows a single continuous path from the left edge to the resting place with no gaps or backtracking. The drawing keeps the same size in every frame.
primary_gap: While the two birds cross the frame edges in frames 4-6, short cut-off stroke pieces are left near the edges (small dashes at the left edge of frame 4 and loose fragments at the right edge of frame 5) instead of clean partial drawings.
closes_when: In e.png frames 4-6 every visible black mark at a frame edge belongs to a continuous partial outline of one of the two birds, with no detached dashes.
protect: The two-bird pan matching the film (one bird exiting right in frames 1-5 while the second enters from the left in frames 2-8 at the film's rate); the steady hold from frame 9 on with the small settling drift; the constant drawing size; the head-tucked oval body with the doodle's polygonal head loop, single straight leg, small knee angle and horizontal crossbar; the grey fence and tree scenery moving with the pan.
identity_gap: The doodle's long forward neck and forward-facing head are replaced by a head folded onto the back, which the film's sleeping pose requires, but the oval body, polygonal head loop, single straight leg with angled knee stroke and horizontal crossbar are kept in the doodle's plain line style.
